text:
kai: uploaded a new mock for a 'quickstats ribbon' on model cards. idea: tiny horizontal strip with p95, cost/token, and a compact performance badge. stretch goal: let filters toggle which two metrics show by default. figma link in the thread.
sophia: I like the ribbon, but warning: when density is high the ribbon can push down rows and hurt scan speed. can we make it overlay instead of changing layout?
leo: overlay is fine but z-index complexity on mobile gets weird. alternate: collapse ribbon to icons-only at <540px and show numbers in tooltip.
tan: accessibility: if we overlay, make sure ribbon content is in tab order and has aria-live for metric updates. users with screen readers need context when a metric changes.
beth: UX note from usability session: people wanted the perf badge to be semantically clear. they misinterpreted green check as 'accurate' rather than 'fast'. suggest icon + short label like 'Fast' / 'Balanced' / 'High quality'.
kai: good call. i'll replace check with a tiny label + subtle color. also adding alt text for badges.
sophia: copy tweak: for cost we should avoid $/tk shorthand in the ribbon. use '¢/tk' or 'USD per 1k tk' somewhere accessible. shorthand confused new users.
leo: backend constraint: we can only serve aggregated p95 and cost per model id; per-route breakdowns will be heavy. propose show global model p95 on cards and route-level p95 inside compare modal.
tan: compare UI decision: inline row-expansion vs dedicated compare modal. proposal: keep inline for quick diffs (2 items), auto-suggest modal if user selects 3+ or clicks 'Open full compare'.
beth: participants preferred inline for quick glance, modal for deep dive. also ask: when rows expand inline, highlight the changed metrics with a subtle left stripe color to draw eyes.
sophia: accessibility check: highlight must not rely on color alone. add an icon or text kicker 'changed'. and readable contrast for stripe.
kai: version pinning flow suggestion: instead of 'pin' icon only, show a small 'hold' toggle. states: Unpinned, Hold Major, Hold Exact. tooltip text: 'Hold updates to major versions' or 'Lock to exact model'.
leo: implementation: we need to persist hold state in registry and expose an endpoint to resolve 'Hold Major' to the current canonical minor for running compares. easy enough but we should limit audit events to changes.
tan: keyboard nav: Tab to ribbon, Enter to expand, Arrow keys navigate metrics inside expanded area. ensure aria-expanded toggles and screenreader reads 'Pinned: Hold Major' when relevant.
beth: microcopy suggestion for undo: after changing hold state show toast 'Holding to v3.x · Undo' rather than 'Pinned'. 'Hold' maps better to user mental model.
kai: noted. I'll swap copy to 'Hold' in figma. adding a visual pill showing resolution: e.g., 'Hold v3.x' so it's visible in compare.
sophia: filter chips: when user stacks many filters the chips wrap and push content. recommend an overflow indicator '+3' that opens a scrollable popover of hidden chips.
leo: and performance: rendering many chips should be virtualized. we can lazy-render chips beyond first 12.
tan: screenreader for chip overflow should announce '3 more filters collapsed'. use aria-haspopup on overflow button.
beth: final checklist: overlay ribbon (instead of pushing layout) on desktop, icons-only on small screens, semantic badge labels, 'Hold' pin states with undo toast, inline compare default up to 2 items else modal, chip overflow popover, aria-live and aria-labels for metrics.
kai: I'll update figma + make a PR with the small copy changes and accessibility notes. pinging @design-bot for preview.
design-bot: Preview published: https://figma.redwood.dev/file/quickstats-ribbon-v1  Staging preview: /catalog?preview=quickstats-ribbon (expires in 48h)
sophia: thanks! I'll run a quick 5-person usability check Fri morning and report back.
leo: i'll draft a frontend spike for virtualized chips and overlay ribbon on Monday.
tan: I'll add aria annotations to the design PR so devs have exact strings to use.
beth: thanks all — this reads like a good, incremental rollout path.
